A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain the main text and full supplement. Section moves, figure renumbering, and typesetting differences can be matched without material comparison gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-data simulations and Waterbirds classification experiments, including accuracy and F1 results in Section 5 and Appendices S.3–S.4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, presenting simulations in Section 6 and Waterbirds experiments in Section 7 and Appendix S.3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, target-posterior formulas, KL distribution-matching estimator, weighted-risk procedure, and appendix moment-matching alternative remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same four-dimensional Gaussian synthetic task and Waterbirds under structured subpopulation missingness. Synthetic experiments move into the main text. CelebA remains illustrative in Table 2 rather than an evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same naive source-model comparators: ξ1 and ξ for the synthetic and principal Waterbirds comparisons, and ξ0 for the supplementary A=0 comparison. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Synthetic sample-size grids, known probabilities and proportions, and the 0.5 decision threshold are retained. Waterbirds uses the same allocation-rate sweeps, feature extraction, classifiers, and accuracy/F1 metrics.

E4.justification: Both retain the synthetic sample-size analyses and Waterbirds subgroup-allocation sensitivity analyses, including the a=0.7 settings and A=0 subgroup results. Relocation introduces no new analysis.

E5.justification: Both specify 100 simulations per synthetic configuration and 50 repetitions for Waterbirds, reporting variability through the same boxplots. No uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: The matched figures retain the same plotted results and findings. v1 Figures 2–3 become v2 Figures 1–2, v1 Figure 1 becomes v2 Figure 3, and Figures 4–6 remain. No result entries or numerical outcomes change.

T1.justification: The assumptions, identification results, consistency and generalization bounds, and supplementary proofs are retained. v2 Remarks 1–2 relocate material already in v1 Appendix S.2. Restoring missing loss-symbol glyphs changes typesetting, not mathematical definitions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same recovery, estimation, theoretical-guarantee, and empirical-performance claims. Adding 'for Binary Classification' to the title makes the existing binary scope explicit. The conclusion is relocated without changing its claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of benchmark failures and performance trends are unchanged, as are identifiability qualifications and the discussion of multiclass and environment extensions. v1 Appendix S.5 becomes v2 Section 8 without substantive revision.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same implementation procedure, frozen ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 features, 512-dimensional embeddings, L2-regularized logistic regression, and synthetic oracle calculations. No substantive implementation or resource-access information is added.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to domain adaptation, OOD research, spurious correlations, open-set label shift, and PU learning are retained. Related work and citations accompanying theoretical explanations are relocated.

P1.justification: The narrative structure is substantially reorganized: related work moves before the problem setup, synthetic results and conclusions move from the supplement into dedicated main sections, and two theoretical explanations become main-text remarks. Additional wording edits are limited.

P2.justification: Existing synthetic figures move into the main text and are renumbered; table and plot designs remain substantially unchanged. Title and abstract occupy separate pages, surrounding material reflows, and missing loss-function symbols are restored in definitions, bounds, and proofs.

improvement.justification: v2 improves readability by restoring visibly missing loss-function symbols and placing existing theoretical explanations, simulations, and conclusions in the main narrative. These are useful editorial repairs, while the method, mathematical substance, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
